title: Alpha Has Arrived. After Six Films of Tiger, Pathaan and War, the YRF Spy Universe Finally Belongs to the Women.
excerpt: The trailer opens on an infant in a glass box and ends with Hrithik Roshan stepping out of the shadows. In between, Alia Bhatt and Sharvari turn a male-only franchise upside down — and the whole industry has already taken sides.
body:
An infant, trapped inside a glass enclosure. A man — **Bobby Deol**, cold and unsmiling — leaning in to name her Sita. That is how the **Alpha** trailer opens, and within seconds you understand this is not the spy universe you knew. There are no slow-motion hero entries, no men squinting into desert sunsets. There is a child, a destiny, and a name borrowed from mythology that lands like a loaded gun.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=QRqGwGwo1Y0</youtube>

For six films — three Tigers, a Pathaan, two Wars — Yash Raj Films built India's most lucrative cinematic universe entirely around its leading men. Salman ran. Shah Rukh swam. Hrithik flew. The women looked gorgeous and occasionally fired a weapon. **Alpha**, which dropped its trailer on June 17 and storms into theatres worldwide on **July 3, 2026**, finally tears that script up. This is the franchise's first female-led theatrical venture, and it does not arrive apologetically.

**Alia Bhatt** has never looked like this on screen. Her voiceover narrates the trailer — the story of a princess raised in the dark, drilled through childhood into adulthood until discipline hardens into something lethal. We watch her transform across chase sequences, gun battles, and brutal hand-to-hand combat, leaner and more dangerous than the actress we associate with weepy family dramas and indie character studies. Playing Sita, an operative bred inside a shadowy program called Alpha, she is a revelation in motion.

And then there is **Sharvari**. The makers have done something clever and maddening here: they have kept her character almost entirely under wraps. We get one electric, fleeting confrontation between the two women — the kind of standoff that makes you sit forward — and then nothing. Friend? Foe? Mirror image? The trailer refuses to say, and the not-knowing is exactly the hook YRF wants buried in your skull until July.

The supporting players carry their own weight. **Anil Kapoor**, all silver charisma, appears as the mentor guiding Alia's Sita toward a mission larger than herself. Bobby Deol, fresh off his villain renaissance, plays the mastermind behind the Alpha initiative — a man who appears to turn against the very nation he was meant to protect. Driving the adrenaline underneath it all is global chart-topper **HUGEL**'s 'Jamaican Bam Bam,' a pulsating needle-drop that gives the cut a slick, almost European-thriller cool.

Then comes the moment that broke the internet. In the dying seconds of the trailer, the screen confirms what fans had only whispered about: **Hrithik Roshan**'s Kabir, from *War*, is making a special appearance. The interconnected machinery of the YRF Spy Universe clicks into place, and suddenly Alpha is not a spin-off — it is canon, the seventh chapter of a saga that already includes *Tiger*, *Pathaan*, and *War*.

The industry reaction was instant and effusive. **Karan Johar** posted the trailer to his Instagram Stories with his usual maximalist flourish:

> "This rock and roll actioner screams GIRLPOWER in the best way! @aliaabhatt and @sharvari are on a mission to Block a Buster! OG energy with @anilskapoor and @iambobbydeol! Shiv Rawail makes his bada screen debut with a BANG!" — Karan Johar

**Sonam Kapoor** was among the first to weigh in, and she went straight for the genre's long-standing gender gap:

> "So cool to see a Bollywood film that puts girls at the centre of an action entertainer! High time this happened and honestly why should boys have all the fun doing action?!" — Sonam Kapoor

She is right, and the subtext is hard to miss. Hindi cinema's most bankable genre — the big-budget, all-guns-blazing actioner — had quietly stayed a boys' club for decades. Alpha is the reckoning.

Directed by **Shiv Rawail**, who earned serious critical respect for the streaming series *The Railway Men*, and produced by **Aditya Chopra**, the film blends emotional origin-story stakes with the large-scale spectacle the franchise is built on. The screenplay comes from Soumil Shukla and Shridhar Raghavan.

For the diaspora, the good news is that this is a worldwide theatrical release. Expect **Alpha** in cinemas across the US, UK, Canada, and the Gulf on July 3 — the usual overseas YRF rollout through AMC, Cineworld, and Cineplex chains, with subtitled prints standard for these tentpoles. A streaming home will almost certainly follow on Amazon Prime Video, where YRF has parked its recent library, though no date has been announced.

Two deadly girls, one glass box, and a universe that just doubled its possibilities. The hunt begins July 3.
